title: John Lennon’s Bag One exhibition is raided by Oak Brook police | 1970
content:
Bag One, John Lennon’s exhibition of erotic lithographs, was raided by police in Oak Brook police on 28 March 1970.

The lithographs, known collectively as Bag One, had been drawn by Lennon in 1969, and chronicled his wedding ceremony and honeymoon with Yoko Ono, and one of their bed-ins for world peace. The Bag One Portfolio was published as a limited edition of 300, and contained 14 artworks. Each lithograph was signed by Lennon.

The Oak Brook exhibition was at the Merrill Chase Gallery in Oak Brook, Illinois, USA. Similar exhibitions had opened in London (15 January), Detroit (21 January), Long Beach (28 January), New York City (7 February), Amsterdam (7 February), San Francisco (13 February), Toronto (14 February), Milan (20 February), Los Angeles (1 March), and Dusseldorf (14 March).

The Oak Brook exhibition was restricted to over 21s, but law enforcement officers entered with a search warrant and confiscated the offending. Following a court hearing, DuPage County chief circuit judge Bert J Rathje found five of the works to be obscene and ordered them to be burnt. The burning took place on 3 June 1970.

Lennon’s Bag One exhibition in London had been raided by police on 16 January.
